title: The completeness check
intro: This round is about the Pre-Authorization check: how its result reads to a doctor, how readiness is shown, and what a person settles by hand. Requests to departments come in Round 8.

questions.question: When a treating doctor opens a Case File, how should the Pre-Authorization result first appear?

options.label: One line plus to-do list (Recommended)
options.description: Shows '6 of 9 ready' and only the 3 things left, each with who acts; the full record list opens on tap.

options.label: Full record table
options.description: Every required record at once with its status, as today but simplified; more to read before the first action.

options.label: Single colour badge
options.description: Green, amber or red only; the reason is always one tap away.

questions.why: Sets how the check opens for a first-time doctor. Today the tab lists Level 1 gaps, Level 2 gaps, met records and 'shown, not counted' with jargon on every row (U16, U01; J1 friction: three long paragraphs before the first button). I16 next-step card liked; Hartmann 2026: 55% of preparation time is spent on the system.

questions.question: How many different states should a doctor see for a required record?

options.label: Ready, needs you, waiting (Recommended)
options.description: Records sort by who acts: ready; needs you (attest, confirm, failed document); waiting on a department or the HIS. The exact reason is one line under it.

options.label: All nine statuses
options.description: Missing, not final, needs confirmation, missing value, needs review, pending, blocked, waived and met each keep their own chip and colour.

options.label: Ready or not ready
options.description: One chip per record; the reason is plain text, so colour carries less meaning.

questions.why: PreAuth_Checks_for_Validation.pdf (sent to the doctors) lists 9 checks with red, amber, violet and grey statuses plus 'Pending' and 'Gate blocked'. U05 (one word per state), U19 (status shown three times on one row), I17 plain names.

questions.question: Should the words 'Level 1' and 'Level 2' stay in the check?

options.label: Drop them, plain words (Recommended)
options.description: Rows say 'report missing', 'report not final or not signed', 'value not found in the report'; the two levels live only in the code.

options.label: Rename to Reports and Values
options.description: Two groups: 'Reports in place' (present, final, signed, right patient) and 'Values found' (with a quote).

options.label: Keep Level 1 / Level 2
options.description: Same as today, with a one-line meaning on hover; doctors learn the terms once.

questions.why: Level 1 = record present, final, signed, right patient; Level 2 = required values present with a verified quote (B4, data.js glossary). U16 calls it jargon; U04: the in-app glossary defines the levels differently from the code (Case File vs single record). R01 sets terminology in general; this is the check's own wording.

questions.question: How should readiness be shown on a Case File, given your rule that a progress bar should not start from 0?

options.label: Journey bar of real steps (Recommended)
options.description: The bar counts the path (created, records fetched, check met, summary, ready), so it starts part-full honestly; '6 of 9 records ready' sits beside it.

options.label: Bar of records ready
options.description: Fills by records ready out of records required; fetched records count at once, but a new patient can still show 0.

options.label: Fixed 20% head start
options.description: Starts at 20% for creating the Case File and spreads the records over the rest; the bar no longer equals records ready divided by required.

options.label: Count only, no bar
options.description: Text such as '6 of 9 ready'; nothing to misread, less sense of momentum.

questions.why: UX_notes.md point 5 (progress bar not from 0). Today readiness % = records satisfied / records that apply, waived records leave the count (validation sheet page 1). The coordinator's readiness list (B15) shows the same number, so the choice carries over to R10.

questions.question: Must the Pre-Authorization check be met before the owner can mark a Case File ready for the board?

options.label: Met, or each gap settled (Recommended)
options.description: Ready only when every required record is met, waived or marked not applicable with a reason; no silent gap reaches the agenda.

options.label: No, advice only
options.description: The owner may mark ready with gaps, as the code allows today; the gaps show to the coordinator and the board.

options.label: Gaps only with urgent reason
options.description: Ready with gaps needs an 'urgent case' reason, audited and shown on the agenda and in the room.

questions.why: Today mark_ready (board.py) needs only a protocol and a board date, not a met check, while the summary needs a met check (V2 4.4). Research: 24% of UK lung MDT cases deferred, mostly awaiting results; NHS England 2020 puts responsibility for complete information on the referring clinician. R10 then decides who marks ready and the agenda rules.

questions.question: Should 'not applicable' be a separate action from 'waive'?

options.label: Two actions, both with reason (Recommended)
options.description: 'Not applicable' when a record does not fit this patient (mammography in a man); 'Waive' when it fits but the board goes ahead without it.

options.label: One 'Not needed' button
options.description: One action with a short reason list (not applicable, patient declined, done elsewhere, urgent) plus free text.

options.label: Keep 'Waive' only
options.description: As today: one waive with a free-text reason, removed from the count.

questions.why: Validation sheet check 9 (waived, grey; logged, removed from the count). T09 Cancer of Unknown Primary plans records conditional on sex and presentation with 'not applicable' and a reason (W4). Checkpoints table: waive needs a reason today.

questions.question: Should waiving an NCG Essential record need anything more than a reason?

options.label: Reason, shown to the board (Recommended)
options.description: No second approval; the waiver and its reason appear in the summary, on the agenda line and in the room.

options.label: Second consultant approves
options.description: Another consultant of the owning department (or its head) approves before the waiver counts; slower, two names on it.

options.label: Reason only, as today
options.description: Logged and audited, but the board sees it only if someone opens the audit.

questions.why: Essential (tier a) records are required at every hospital (validation sheet Part 2). Today a waiver needs only a reason and is audited (checkpoints). Links to 'expert over the loop' (R01) and to the board seeing what is missing (I01 presenter mode gap badges).

questions.question: In the check, what may a resident, PG or fellow do on a Case File they joined?

options.label: Propose; consultant approves (Recommended)
options.description: Every attest, confirm, waive or not-applicable a resident makes stays 'proposed' until the treating doctor approves; the audit shows both names.

options.label: Small confirmations alone
options.description: Resident confirms report dates and document type alone; attest final, waive, patient match and values from scans need the consultant.

options.label: View and chase only
options.description: Resident sees the check and sends requests but cannot confirm or waive anything.

questions.why: Settled: residents join a Case File with a code and cannot sign 'same as PACS systems' (notes role-treating, role-resident); I03 liked (drafts, consultant approves, both names). B5 lists the person-only actions. R03 sets resident rights overall; this asks only about the check's actions.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R03 already set resident rights for attest, confirm and waive.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R03-Q04 (the general resident sign-off rule covers attest, confirm and waive).

questions.question: May the treating doctor type a required value into Vaidyx when no signed report carries it?

options.label: Only the board question (Recommended)
options.description: The question for the board is typed on the Case File with the doctor's name; every other required value must come from a signed report.

options.label: Board question and clinical values
options.description: Also ECOG and menopausal status, each shown as 'entered by Dr X, no report'; fewer requests, more values without a report quote.

options.label: Nothing typed
options.description: Every value must be quoted from a signed report; a missing value means a request or a waiver.

questions.why: The clinical-history record requires 'ECOG performance status' and 'Question for the Tumour Board' quoted from a clinical note (validation sheet Part 3); HIS notes rarely carry the board question, so the owner ends up requesting it from itself (G12). Greater Manchester pro-forma makes the clinical question mandatory; I07. Invariant: a value shown as fact needs a verified quote, so a typed value is shown as the doctor's own statement.

questions.question: For records needed only in some patients (bronchoscopy if surgery is planned, PSA only in men), who settles whether they apply?

options.label: Doctor answers yes or no (Recommended)
options.description: The Case File asks short questions such as 'Surgery planned?'; the answer turns the record on or off, audited. Sex and age come from registration.

options.label: Optional, never blocking
options.description: Conditional records are shown for information only, as today; the doctor remembers which apply.

options.label: Required until marked not applicable
options.description: Every conditional record blocks until it is met or marked not applicable with a reason.

questions.why: Lung bronchoscopy 'patients planned for surgery', MRI thorax 'superior sulcus tumour only' and oral cavity PET-CT 'high risk' are Optional today because the system must not judge the condition (validation sheet Part 3; scope). T09 CUP needs records conditional on sex and presentation.

questions.question: On each required record, how much of its guideline source should show?

options.label: Short chip, quote on tap (Recommended)
options.description: 'NCG Breast 2019, p 5' on the row; a tap shows the guideline's exact line and opens that page in the library.

options.label: Full quote always visible
options.description: The guideline line shows under every row; complete but long on a phone.

options.label: Separate sources page
options.description: Rows show no source; one 'Why these records' page lists every record with its guideline line.

questions.why: T10 kept with 'only validated sources'; W1 'a justification for whatever you are listing'. Every protocol record already carries its NCG guideline, page and verbatim quote (V1 4.1); the rectal rows show 'p.n/a' on the validation sheet. R01 decides what counts as a validated source and the general source style.
depends_on: R01 (validated sources and how they are shown)
questions.skip_if: Skip if R01 fixed one source display for every screen.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R01-Q08 (one source display for every screen).

questions.question: If the check stops being met after a Case File was marked ready (an amended report, a changed stage group), what should happen?

options.label: Keep on agenda, warn both (Recommended)
options.description: The ready mark stays with 'check no longer met: CT amended'; the owner and the coordinator are told at once.

options.label: Remove the ready mark
options.description: The Case File leaves 'ready' until the check is met again; the coordinator is told and may drop it from the agenda.

options.label: Nothing until the meeting
options.description: The change shows only when someone opens the Case File.

questions.why: The check re-runs by itself in milliseconds after every re-fetch, confirmation or setting change (B4, B8); an amended report becomes the current version. Today the ready mark does not react. R10 (agenda cut-off) and R14 (who hears what) build on this.

questions.question: When two final reports disagree on a value that should not change (HER2, histologic type), should the check wait for a doctor?

options.label: Wait until a doctor notes (Recommended)
options.description: The check is not met until a doctor opens both quotes and notes the disagreement (audited); it then goes to the board as a Point for review.

options.label: Flag only, never block
options.description: As today: shown in 'Reports that disagree' and the summary; the check can be met without anyone looking.

questions.why: 12 Oct discordance check (OCT12_FEATURES.md 3): stable fields that differ between final reports are 'for review', a polarity flip is always review; today they never block. Noting is audited and undoable. Vaidyx never says which value is right; the board decides.

questions.question: Can you get the hospital's current Tumour Board case submission form or checklist, blank, with no patient data?

options.label: I'll get it (Recommended)
options.description: We compare its fields with the NCG-based record list and the typed board question before the check is rebuilt.

options.label: Skip for now
options.description: The check stays NCG-based only; hospital fields are added later.

options.label: Use a published pro-forma
options.description: We model the typed fields on the Greater Manchester MDT standards pro-forma, already in the research.

questions.why: No hospital form is held (RESOURCES.md lists guidelines and synoptic templates only). It shows which fields the doctors already fill by hand (board question, ECOG, consent, specimen numbers), which settles R07-Q09 against real practice.

resource.item: The hospital's blank Tumour Board case submission form or checklist (no patient data)
resource.source_url: No public URL: the hospital's Tumour Board secretariat, through Dr Minmini (Radiology) or Dr Usha (Biochemistry); fallback https://gmcancer.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/V3.0-GM-MDT-Standards-June-23.pdf
resource.why: Aligns the check's required fields and the typed values with what the hospital's board already asks for.
